summary: Outstanding refund reversals are never retried automatically (TKT-157 follow-up)
description:
Found by the TKT-157 adversarial review (finding F3). Recorded rather than fixed there, for the reasons in ADR-038 §7.

A refund whose money moved but whose tickets were not voided — access down, `ACCESS_URL` unset, or issuance not caught up (503) — is **visible** (`order_refunds.tickets_voided_at IS NULL`) and **retryable** (replay the same idempotency key). Nothing retries it. The reviewer's sharpest point: the caller receives an HTTP **200**, so there is no signal telling it to come back, and the outstanding obligation depends on someone noticing `tickets_voided:false`.

TKT-157's AC asked for *visible and retryable*, which is met. Automatic retry is a different requirement, and a second recovery state machine in commerce is a large cost to add on the strength of a review finding rather than a stated need — so it was deferred here, not dismissed. TKT-161 adds `capacity_returned_at` as a second outstanding obligation of the same shape, which is the natural moment to decide whether one runner should drive both.

Related in kind: **TKT-146** (no operator path to resolve or unpark a parked recovery order).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] An outstanding reversal is driven to completion without a human replaying the request, or there is an explicitly monitored, documented reconciler that is part of the deployment contract.
- [ ] Whatever drives it is idempotent against the downstream operations, which already are.
- [ ] A test drives a downstream outage and proves the obligation completes afterwards.
- [ ] Decide, and record, whether missing `ACCESS_URL` should become a readiness failure — ADR-038 §7 currently makes it a deliberate degradation.

Quality gates: `make check` green; contract tests; money untouched.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.

Traceability is a must, for money and tickets: money-relevant records land as immutable, hash-chained, signed journal entries from the first order (corrections = compensating entries; read models = projections), and every ticket/entitlement state change (issued, delivered, transferred, resold, exchanged, redeemed, reissued, invalidated) is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order.

governingAdrs.why: Every lifecycle event goes through store.appendLifecycle — the verifier asserts one-to-one coverage, so a direct INSERT into lifecycle_events reads as tampering and fails `access verify-lifecycle` in the gate. Canonical forms are pinned by golden literals; changing a byte is a canonical-version migration, not a test update. Also: name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'.

Inventory's claim transaction is the contention path. Giving capacity back must go through the same row-locked transaction discipline; a plain UPDATE outside it can drive confirmed_quantity negative or double-return under concurrency.
Capacity adjustments clamp rather than reject. Returning capacity must not let availability exceed the pool's capacity, and the clamp reasoning is the precedent for what to do when it would.

Corrections are COMPENSATING ENTRIES, never mutations. A refund/exchange appends a new signed fact; the original sale fact and its hash link are untouched. The payments journal has a DB trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE — any design that 'adjusts' a fact is rejected by the database, not by review.

If any domain event payload changes or a new one is published: bump on CONSUMER SEMANTICS, not parse compatibility, and consumers dispatch on `schema` BEFORE decoding `data`. A fixture built from the type under test cannot fail.

Fail closed. Responses are validated against the spec; an undeclared status code becomes a 500. Every new endpoint must declare every status it can answer, and a downstream answer commerce cannot validate aborts rather than degrades.

Contract-first. A new operation is written in the service's openapi.yaml first, then `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and COMMITTED before the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Commerce and inventory ARE inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate. A new documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.

Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job. Add the SQL under the service's internal/store/migrations/ with the next number; the server path never migrates.

objective.note: A transient access outage currently leaves refunded tickets valid until a human replays the refund.

scope.note: IN: driving outstanding reversal obligations to completion. OUT: the money path, which is already durable and already recovered.

uncertainties.note: Runner vs outbox vs external reconciler is a Planning-time call. Best taken after TKT-161, when both obligations exist and one mechanism can cover both.

dependencies.note: Not blocked, but worth sequencing after TKT-161 so the design covers both obligations rather than being retrofitted.

first_slice.note: Drive the ticket-voiding obligation after a simulated access outage.

success.note: Demoable: stop access, refund, restart access, watch the reversal complete with no human action.

context_memo.note: Inherited from TKT-157; ADR-038 §7 records the rejected design and why.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Shapeable now, better after TKT-161. Two obligations of identical shape will exist then, and deciding the mechanism against one of them risks a design that has to be retrofitted for the second.

**Concerns:** (1) sequencing, above. (2) The `ACCESS_URL`-as-readiness question is a deployment-contract decision, not purely engineering.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — proceedable, but hold for TKT-161.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 — promoted to Ready (owner, 2026-08-17)

**Outstanding refund reversals are never retried automatically.**

Its deferral has now been *satisfied*, which is why it is promotable. `uncertainties`,
`dependencies` and `approach` were all deferred with one shared reason: *"best taken after TKT-161,
when both obligations exist and one mechanism can cover both."* **TKT-161 is Done.** The condition
the deferral named has been met, so the Planning-time call (runner vs outbox vs external
reconciler) can now be taken against both obligations rather than retrofitted to one.

**On `approach: deferred` and the money-path carve-out** — `shaping.md` says a deferred approach
does *not* pass when a ticket touches money. Called out rather than glossed: the exception does not
bite here, because what is deferred is a **mechanism choice among three known options**, not a
decision about who may spend or what a trust boundary is. The obligation is already visible
(`order_refunds.tickets_voided_at IS NULL`) and already retryable by replaying the idempotency key.
If Planning finds the choice is actually about authorization, that is a signal to stop and
re-shape.

**Verified before promoting, not assumed:** all eight DoR items are `met` or `deferred` with none
`open`, and every `blocked-by` link resolves to a **Done** ticket. Promoted as part of a sweep of
every fully-shaped Backlog ticket, on the owner's instruction.
